subject: Post-call recap: Redwood integration & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Priya Gupta <priya.gupta@acme.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: Redwood integration & next steps

Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks again for the call earlier — appreciate the context on the search and chat experiences you’re trying to unify. Quick recap from our side and suggested next steps.

High-level pain points you mentioned
- Unpredictable latency spikes on your current hosted solution during peak traffic (affects user experience for live chat).
- High unit cost for embeddings + reranking at your current traffic levels — need to reduce per-query spend.
- Need for structured outputs from the model (JSON) to reliably populate downstream services.
- Desire to stream partial responses into the UI while also retaining the ability to call internal APIs (function calling) for actions (e.g., ticket create, KB lookup).
- Security constraints: SSO + customer-managed keys for pilot, and audit logs retained for 12 months.

What Redwood can help with (short list)
- Streaming responses + SDK support to render partial tokens in your chat UI with early actionable suggestions.
- Function calling so the model can deterministically trigger internal APIs (we support typed schemas and SDK helpers).
- Embeddings + reranking pipeline recommendations (we suggested dense embeddings + an FAISS index with periodic re-rerank and caching of top results).
- Cost controls: batching, prefix caching, and quantization profiles for pilot to bring down per-token cost.
- Private deployment options (VPC) for the pilot if you need customer-managed keys.

Proposed next steps
1) Technical deep-dive w/ your engineering & our solutions engineer (1h) — suggested Thurs 11/12 or Fri 11/13.
2) Scope pilot: 6-week pilot targeting chat with streaming + embeddings rerank. Goal: 30% RMSE reduction in latency tail + 20% unit cost reduction vs current baseline.
3) SOW + pilot milestones draft — attaching a one-page recap and a rough SOW template for your review.

Attachments: redwood-acme-discovery-recap.pdf (summary), redwood-pilot-sow-v1.docx (draft).

If that all looks right, I’ll lock in a time for the deep-dive and loop in Dev.

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | (415) 555-0123

Thanks Marissa — this is helpful. A few clarifying items from our side: 

1) Pilot scope: when you say "embeddings + reranking pipeline," can you confirm whether the canonical approach will be (a) host embeddings in Redwood and use a managed vector index, or (b) produce embeddings and push to our existing hosted FAISS cluster? We prefer (b) because we have operational monitoring around our index.

2) Function calling: Is there a recommended schema format you support? We need strong typing so our backend can validate actions before execution.

3) Streaming: Important that partial tokens are returned with a stable token order — we had issues with interrupted streams in our previous integration.

4) Pricing & pilot terms: can you share a baseline estimate for expected cost for a 6-week pilot (ballpark)? Also what SLA would apply for a reserved pilot?

We can do the technical deep-dive on Thurs 11/12 10am PT — that works for our eng leads.

Alex
Senior Product Manager | Acme Corp
alex.johnson@acme.com

Alex — great questions, answers inline below and added a few technical notes.

1) Embeddings + index: both options are supported. For the pilot we recommend option (b) — produce embeddings via Redwood and push vectors to your FAISS cluster. That preserves your monitoring and gives you control over the index. We’ll provide a small script and SDK helper to reliably upsert and version vectors.

2) Function calling schema: we support OpenAPI-style schemas and a simplified typed JSON schema for quick iteration. Our SDK validates inputs against the schema before sending the model request, and we include a dry-run mode to show the call the model would make without executing.

3) Streaming stability: our streaming path guarantees token order and offers reconnection semantics (client receives a resume token). We’ll share the SDK example during the deep-dive — the streaming + function-calling example is something we demo often.

4) Pricing & SLA: rough pilot estimate — for the expected profile you described (150k queries / week, average 75 tokens generated / call, embeddings batch 10k docs): estimate ~$18k–$25k for the 6-week pilot with reserved burst capacity. SLA: we can offer a 99.5% availability target for Dedicated pilot capacity; hosted pilots get 99.0% with regional failover. I’ll follow-up with an itemized estimate in the SOW.

Next steps (confirming)
- Tech deep-dive Thurs 11/12 10am PT — I’ll send a calendar invite and include our solutions engineer (Dev).
- I’ll attach a short technical agenda + starter SOW draft for your review.
- After the deep-dive we’ll propose a pilot kickoff date and milestone plan.

Attachments: redwood-technical-deep-dive-agenda.pdf, redwood-pilot-sow-v1.docx

Thanks — looking forward to it.

Best,
Marissa
